title: Veil and Sigil
premise: Astrid Joubert has spent his life mapping the unmapped from the safety of the valley, where a centuries-old ward suppresses all magic—including his own gift of seeing the true shape of places. When the usurper King Aldric declares a realm-wide hunt for the gifted, refugees flood into the valley and shatter Astrid's invisibility: among them is Sera, whose soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain to buy her family's passage. To save her—and the free cities that depend on her knowledge of the old roads—Astrid must leave the valley for the first time, leading a ragtag found family through realms only he can chart. At the mountain's heart he discovers the court trades souls to fuel Aldric's armies, and he must choose between buying Sera's back with his own gift or exposing the court's ledger to the world. He does both, at terrible cost: the valley's ward breaks, magic returns to the lowlands, and Astrid—no longer a mapmaker of safe distances—becomes the cartographer of a new, unhidden world.
about_author: Paloma Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval route-maps before turning to fiction full-time. They write fantasy about people who make their homes in the margins, and live in a drafty house full of atlases they refuse to organize.

chapters.title: The Valley That Refuses
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. We meet him drafting maps of places he can never visit, guided by letters and rumor, while the valley's ward hums faintly at its borders. A routine survey reveals the ward flickering for the first time in living memory. Emotional beat: quiet unease—the safety he's built may already be eroding.

chapters.title: Ink and Ordinary Days
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Daily life in the valley: his mentor Odile, the tavern debates, his careful habit of hiding small oddities of perception. News arrives by peddler of King Aldric's edict—a hunt for anyone with the gift. Emotional beat: dread arriving gently, disguised as gossip.

chapters.title: Refugees at the Ford
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The first refugees cross the ford, and with them something changes: inside the valley, Astrid can suddenly see the true shape of things—the gift the ward once suppressed waking as it strains. Among the arrivals: Sera, hollow-eyed, guarded. Emotional beat: wonder tangled with guilt.

chapters.title: What Sera Sold
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. She reveals her secret to Astrid alone: to smuggle her family past Aldric's checkpoints, she sold her soul to the court beneath the mountain. Now she feels herself thinning—forgetting her mother's face. Emotional beat: shame met, unexpectedly, with compassion rather than judgment.

chapters.title: The Council of Small Voices
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The valley's council debates turning refugees away to avoid Aldric's attention; Odile argues for shelter, an elder for exile. Astrid, voice shaking, speaks for staying invisible no longer being survival. Emotional beat: first act of courage—choosing a side publicly.

chapters.title: King's Men at the Border
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Aldric's inquisitors arrive at the valley's edge, probing the ward. Astrid uses his waking gift to read the ward's structure and quietly reinforce it—but the effort burns through his anonymity. One inquisitor marks his face. Emotional beat: the cost of competence.

chapters.title: The Ledger Beneath
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. A dying refugee, once a clerk of the mountain court, describes the soul-ledger: every sold soul recorded, every one feeding the usurper's war engines. Sera learns her soul powers a siege foundry bound for the free cities. Emotional beat: horror sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Leaving the Map
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid decides to leave the valley—to guide a small company to the mountain and steal Sera's soul back before the foundry marches. Odile gives him her old compass and a warning: outside, his gift will be both weapon and beacon. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of the threshold.

chapters.title: The Company of Strays
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The party forms: Sera, the ex-clerk Bramble, disgraced soldier Yorick, and twin scouts Fen and Ost. Friction over trust, routes, and secrets. Astrid maps their first night's camp and realizes he's drawing people, not just terrain. Emotional beat: awkward beginnings of belonging.

chapters.title: Roads That Remember
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. In the wilds, Astrid's gift deepens—he perceives old roads and buried ways invisible to others, guiding them past a checkpoint that should have caught them. But each use sends ripples other gifted folk can feel. Emotional beat: power as double-edged intimacy with the land.

chapters.title: The Free City of Vell
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Resupply in Vell: markets, spies, and proof of Aldric's approaching armies. Sera sees how the free cities could hold—if warned in time—and understands her stolen soul is a strategic weapon, not just a personal wound. Emotional beat: private grief reframed as public stakes.

chapters.title: Yorick's Confession
chapters.summary: Yorick's POV. Around the fire, Yorick admits he served Aldric's purge before deserting; he joined the company seeking penance. Sera must decide whether loyalty or truth governs the group. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh—can honesty cost less than betrayal?

chapters.title: Ambush on the Gray Stair
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Inquisitors, tracking Astrid's ripples, ambush the company on a cliff road. Fen is gravely wounded; Astrid, cornered, uses his gift openly for the first time—folding the terrain to save them. Emotional beat: victory shadowed by exposure; there is no going back.

chapters.title: What the Gift Costs
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Aftermath: Astrid is feverish, his sense of place fraying—he nearly loses himself in the landscape. Sera nurses him and shares what thinning feels like; two damaged people recognize each other. Emotional beat: tenderness born of mutual damage.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The company descends through dwarven ruins into the court: a cathedral of ledgers where souls burn as fuel. They pose as tribute-bearers. Astrid reads the architecture like a map and finds the vault. Emotional beat: awe curdling into cold anger.

chapters.title: The Price of a Name
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Negotiation with the Court's Steward: a soul can be bought back—but the price is another. The Steward names Astrid's gift as fair payment. Sera refuses to let him pay; Astrid secretly begins planning to pay anyway. Emotional beat: love as argument against sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Third Option
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. Bramble, the ex-clerk, proposes heresy: don't buy or barter—erase. If the ledger entry is struck, the soul returns to its owner and the court loses its claim. It requires reaching the master ledger under guard. Emotional beat: hope built on audacity rather than exchange.

chapters.title: Heist of the Hollow Choir
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The infiltration: Yorick creates a diversion, the twins cut the wards, Astrid navigates blind corridors by feel, Sera confronts her own recorded name. They strike the entry—but alarms sing through the mountain. Emotional beat: triumph interrupted mid-breath.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Shadow
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Fleeing upward, they find Aldric himself has come to the court to collect his war-fuel. Confrontation: he offers Astrid a place as royal cartographer—legitimacy in exchange for betrayal of the free cities' roads. Emotional beat: temptation articulated perfectly, and refused.

chapters.title: Ledger and Fire
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Climax. Rather than flee, Astrid turns his gift on the court itself, mapping its hidden structure to the fleeing refugees and the free cities—exposing the soul-trade to the world. The court collapses; Sera's soul returns; Aldric's armies lose their fuel. Odile's compass shatters. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, paid for in blood and light.

chapters.title: The Ward Breaks
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Homecoming to a changed valley: with the court destroyed, the old ward fails, and magic floods the lowlands. Some fear it; the refugees begin to build instead of hide. Sera, whole again, teaches others to guard their names. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into stewardship.

chapters.title: Cartographer of the Unhidden World
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Epilogue. Astrid publishes the first honest map of the realm—every road, every hidden court, nothing veiled. His found family gathers as he inks the final border. He signs it not with his name, but with theirs. Emotional beat: found family as the true territory; home redrawn.
